title: UCP identity linking: OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE
summary: To act for a signed-in buyer (orders, saved addresses, loyalty), the platform links the buyer account at the business with OAuth 2.0. It finds the authorization server through protected-resource and authorization-server metadata, runs the authorization code flow with PKCE S256, and requests scopes derived from capabilities. Three access levels exist: public, agent-authenticated and user-authenticated.

steps.label: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
steps.detail: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata names the authorization server.

steps.label: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
steps.detail: RFC 8414 metadata; the platform falls back to /.well-known/openid-configuration only on 404. The issuer must match byte for byte.

failures.outcome: The platform must stop; the metadata may be spoofed.

steps.label: Redirect to authorize (PKCE S256, capability scopes)
steps.detail: Scopes come from capabilities, for example dev.ucp.shopping.order:read and dev.ucp.shopping.checkout:manage. Plain PKCE must not be used.

payload.content:
# Illustrative example, spec version 2026-08-25.
GET /authorize?response_type=code&client_id=https%3A%2F%2Fagent.example%2Fclient&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fagent.example%2Fcb&scope=dev.ucp.shopping.order%3Aread%20dev.ucp.shopping.checkout%3Amanage&code_challenge=E9Melhoa2Ow...&code_challenge_method=S256&state=af0ifjsldkj HTTP/1.1
Host: accounts.shop.example

steps.label: Sign in and consent at the business
steps.detail: The buyer authenticates with the business, not with the platform.

steps.label: Redirect with code and iss
steps.detail: The business must return iss (RFC 9207) and enforce exact redirect_uri matching.

steps.label: Token request with code_verifier
steps.detail: The platform exchanges the code for tokens. In the accelerated IdP flow of v2026-08-25, the platform instead presents a JWT grant from a trusted IdP (RFC 8693 token exchange, RFC 7523 bearer grant) and never forwards a raw IdP token.

steps.label: User-authenticated call, e.g. GET /orders/{id}
steps.detail: Platform credentials plus the user token give the user-authenticated access level. Businesses must support RFC 7009 token revocation and should support OpenID RISC account events.

failures.outcome: identity_required (401) with a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge.
